summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, and a history of bilateral lower extremity amputations was admitted for shakiness and nausea, symptoms she had previously experienced during urinary tract infections. She had not had her Foley catheter changed in 1.5 weeks, and urinalysis showed bacteria and white blood cells, though she remained afebrile with normal white blood cell count. Symptoms improved rapidly after initial antibiotic administration in the emergency department, suggesting a possible anxiety component or medication effect. Gabapentin, which can accumulate in renal failure and cause tremors, was discontinued during admission and restarted at a lower dose upon discharge. She received scheduled hemodialysis, which improved her renal function and electrolytes. Repeat urine culture showed gram-negative rods and yeast, but due to lack of systemic infection signs, antibiotics were not continued to avoid promoting multidrug-resistant organisms. She was discharged home with services, with follow-up planned for pending culture results and ongoing management of chronic conditions.
